summary: Envelope release is on (ENVELOPE_RELEASE): a member releases old envelope payloads as #6965 describes, while every peer it exchanged with in the last 14 days takes signed claims (signed-claims-v1). While one does not, release pauses and the replication status lists it (envelope_release_paused_for). On a copy of a 52 GB member it released 52,092 envelopes and gave back 0.29 GB with every digest equal; the 9.38 GB of payload whose claims still lack their writers' signatures comes back as each peer signs its own claims (S2c).

replay.detail: No replay. Readers already read released envelopes (#6965).

schema.detail: New table peer_signed_claims (peer, whether its last exchange took signed claims, when), written when a peer's answer changes and otherwise at most hourly. Storage version 28 (envelope_release::ENVELOPES_RELEASED_VERSION) commits in the transaction that first releases an envelope or first admits a signed one; MAX_SUPPORTED_STORAGE_VERSION is 28. A store at 28, like one at 27, stores no valid replica record for a claim it admits from then on; deleting the valid records it already holds stays off (VALID_RECORD_DELETION).

compatibility.detail: Release waits for older peers: while any peer this member exchanged with in the last 14 days sends an inventory without signed-claims-v1, nothing is released, and envelope_release_paused_for in the replication status names those peers. A peer counts from its own exchanges, inbound or answered, with no coordination; one not heard from for 14 days no longer counts. A peer that takes signed claims gets released envelopes' claims as signed claims, and an older one still gets every envelope this member holds.

downtime.detail: No startup work beyond creating the table. The release pass runs in the background after open: it judges envelopes on a reader, 50 ms a page, and each write releases at most 8 within 10 ms of work, then the freed pages go back 128 at a time.

recovery.detail: Rollback is supported until this member first releases an envelope or admits a signed one: until then the store keeps its storage version and peer_signed_claims is ignored by earlier builds. From then on the store is at version 28, and every earlier build refuses to open it, the release with #6965 included; roll forward, or restore a backup taken with fractal backup create before the upgrade. Release starts only once every recent peer takes signed claims, so a fleet rolling back together before that point loses nothing.
